verdict.rationale: Plaid's data access is split into separate products (Auth, Balance, Identity, Transactions), and the Sandbox endpoint takes an explicit list of 'initial products', which implies developers choose which data products to request rather than getting one blanket grant. However, no evidence documents product-scoped user consent screens or explicit data-minimization controls. A community report says the Link flow gave users no indication they were sharing more than account numbers; this is a UX complaint, not a concrete scoping failure, so it lowers confidence rather than creating a dispute. Missing for 10: documentation of per-product consent scoping in Link, documented data-minimization or field-level controls, and independent hands-on confirmation that only the requested scopes are granted.
